description: Out-of-tree explicit spec for the slice-length LAW CONFORMANCE of nim-libp2p's BytesView.toOpenArray on the FIXED template (fix/bytesview-toopenarray-slice-bounds: v.rpos + e - b -> v.rpos + e, one line). The template body (libp2p/utils/bytesview.nim:18-19) now reads v.data.toOpenArray(v.rpos + b, v.rpos + e): at b=1 the underlying inclusive range is [rpos+1, rpos+e], length = e - 1 + 1 = e — EQUAL to the adopted inclusive law e; at b=0 the range [rpos, rpos+e] has length e+1, equal to the law e-0+1, exactly as before the fix (b=0 behavior is byte-identical, which is why the production call sites in noise.nim — all b=0 — are unaffected). Two CONSTRUCTED-IR carriers (the subject is a template): bvSliceLenActual (defect lane, b pinned at 1, model e, adopted law e — the law-conformance obligation (e) == (e) holds for EVERY e in the domain, so NO counterexample exists and no witness is ever selected) and bvSliceLenControl (control, b pinned at 0, model e+1, law e+1; solver-level injection guard). The adopted LAW is DATA, not engine prose: canonicalSpecIR names one law symbol per carrier (bvSliceLenLaw1, bvSliceLenLaw0) and states its body, so the obligation (model == law) is fully determined by this document and the engine hardcodes no law content. A confirmed counterexample would be replayed against the ORIGINAL template through a stamped harness observing len(bv.toOpenArray(1, e)) on BytesView.init(@[byte 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]) — the observation, not the model, decides. The subject tree is READ-ONLY (Zero-Footprint).

semanticCaveats: toOpenArray is a template — the carriers are CONSTRUCTED IR; the solver verifies the ADOPTED MODEL, and the subject connection is the stamped replay harness, which imports libp2p/utils/bytesview and expands the template from the defining module (Nim manual: template symbols are bound from the definition scope)

the adopted law is stated as DATA in canonicalSpecIR (bvSliceLenLaw1 = e at b = 1, bvSliceLenLaw0 = e + 1 at b = 0) — the engine parses the named definitions and hardcodes no law content; the two carriers' obligations are the model-equals-law equalities over the SAME domain variable
the domain 1 <= e <= 5 is bound to the replay fixture BytesView.init(@[byte 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]) with rpos = 0 (a view-relative inclusive [1..e] is valid up to e = 5)
each carrier has exactly ONE model parameter (e); b is fixed at 1 (defect lane) / 0 (control) — a deliberate narrowing required by the single-parameter replay contract

the conformance obligations ((e) == (e) at b = 1, (e + 1) == (e + 1) at b = 0) hold for EVERY e in the domain — the solver finds NO counterexample and the ce-replay lane never fires; the v1.0.0 defect claim ((e - 1) == e, violated for every e) is the historical record over the pre-fix bytes (subject a130a7f3, blob b205c969…)
